sections.title: Policy and access to the centre
sections.text:
Espoo is turning street parking into a charged service around its five centres and its stations. The City Council approved on 8 December 2025, within the 2026 budget, on-street prices of €3.50 an hour in zone 1 and €2.50 in zone 2 from 1 January 2026, with paid spaces to be widened during 2026, mainly near public transport, and an application to raise zone 1 fines from €60 to €80 [3]. On 2 March 2026 the City Board approved the principles for expansion, with zone 1 covering the densely populated area within about 300 m of a centre and zone 2 reaching about 600 m, charges Monday to Friday 8–20 and Saturday 8–18, and in zone 1 also Sundays [0][1]. The city expects the price increase to bring €2.5 million of extra revenue in 2026 and €4.5 million in following years, and park-and-ride prices stay unchanged [1]. It also ended the 50% parking discount for electric cars, with 19 April 2026 the last day [2].

The rollout is by area. Charges take effect as soon as the new signs go up, which started in Kaitaa and Leppävaara in June 2026 and was announced for Tapiola and Otaniemi from October [4][5]. A March 2026 council initiative signed by 26 councillors proposes abolishing mandatory parking-space norms for new buildings, noting that near metro stations Espoo still requires one space per 130 m² or at least 0.5 per dwelling. That is a proposal, not a decision [6]. The Raide-Jokeri light rail began service on 21 October 2023 [17].

sections.title: Parking developments
sections.text:
Park-and-ride is a large part of the supply here. Kivenlahti's park-and-ride, built by Länsimetro, opened on 1 April 2023 with 650 car spaces and 22 charging points, at €2 per 12 hours plus €1 for each extra hour [9]. EuroPark has run Tapiola Park, with 2,000 heated spaces including 370 park-and-ride, since 1 January 2026, and its park-and-ride levels charge €2 for the first 12 hours with an HSL ticket shown [11][12]. The Tapiola Paikoitus page for P-Urheilupuisto lists 200 park-and-ride spaces at €2 per 12 hours with a validated HSL ticket [13]. At Espoonlahti station, both entrances are integrated into the Lippulaiva shopping centre, whose predecessor was demolished in 2017, and the HSL identification device for the park-and-ride was moved in September 2024 to level P2 to ease congestion at the entrances [14][16].

Aalto University began a campus parking pilot at Otaniemi on 1 January 2024, making most outdoor disc-parking areas paid at €1 an hour or €45 a month and opening the Otaparkki car park with 260 paid spaces [8]. We found no sourced figures on garage occupancy or on a shift to shopping centres.

sections.title: Operators, positioning and utilisation
sections.text:
Our Espoo data cover five car parks with 4,309 spaces, all from the Fintraffic feed: Tapiola Park (1,565), Lippulaiva (948), P-Urheilupuisto (796), Kivenlahti (650) and Matinkylä station (350). Capacities in the feed differ from sourced ones: Tapiola Park has 2,000 spaces on its own site, and the page for P-Urheilupuisto gives no total, only 200 park-and-ride spaces [11][13].

Occupancy over August to early October 2026 averaged about 22% on weekdays and 15% at weekends. The fullest is Tapiola Park (32% on weekdays), followed by Matinkylä station (25% on weekdays, falling to 6% at weekends), Lippulaiva (22%) and P-Urheilupuisto (20%). Kivenlahti's park-and-ride reports about 0%, which we cannot explain; the feed may not be counting it. The data cover the summer holidays, so term-time figures may differ, and we have no multi-year history for Espoo.
